pill.desc: clear, colorless solution in a single-dose vial

tell: An erythropoiesis stimulator with a half-life about three times that of epoetin alfa when given intravenously.

clues.text: Subcutaneous bioavailability is 37% in patients on dialysis, and apparent clearance is about 1.4 times faster in dialysis patients than in those not on dialysis.
Produced by recombinant DNA technology in Chinese hamster ovary cells, as a sterile, colorless, preservative-free solution of about 37,000 daltons.
Approved under a BLA as single-dose vials and prefilled syringes, given weekly or once every 2 weeks.

Boxed warning for death, heart attack, stroke, clots and tumor progression. Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension and pure red cell aplasia; hypertension and dyspnea are the most common reactions.
Treating anemia from chronic kidney disease in patients on or off dialysis, and anemia from the effects of concomitant myelosuppressive chemotherapy.
Stimulates red cell production by the same mechanism as the body's own erythropoietin.
The generic name begins with D and has fifteen letters in two words.
